screens.name: Approach
screens.evidence: Sheet 01, approach and transition. A=5.7, F=4.3, overall=4.9; provisional.

screens.name: Home

findings: The orb is an unmistakable hero, with a separate prompt and a restrained omen below.
The entry sample replaces the finished orb with bright unframed texture and hides supporting content; timing and motion comfort remain unverified.

screens.name: Ask — normal text
screens.evidence: Sheets 01–02, ask and transition; supplied runtime reports actual typed submission. A=8.0, F=7.3, overall=7.6; provisional.
findings: Question, alternate voice action and primary submit action are clearly separated.
The large illustrated orb consumes space without displacing the normal-size submit button.
The tilted entry frame weakens input readability; keyboard and focus behavior are unverified.

screens.name: Ask — 200% text

findings: The question wraps legibly, but the orb and enlarged input push both submission choices outside the captured viewport.
The helper paragraph occupies substantial vertical space.
Scrolling may resolve access; this image does not establish an unreachable action.

screens.name: Listening — microphone unavailable

“Speak your question” conflicts with the failed-start state; permission recovery and microphone operation are unverified.

screens.name: Planning — loading

screens.name: Question card 1

screens.name: Question card 3

limitations: Evaluation uses the supplied labeled contact sheets and runtime narrative only. No source, previous grading, other task state or independent runtime inspection was used.
All scores are provisional. Supplied runtime results support bounded task completion; they do not establish every control’s behavior or certify native accessibility.

A is the mean of hierarchy, typography and surfaces; F is the mean of clarity, feedback and accessibility. Truly inapplicable dimensions are excluded. Overall uses unrounded means and is rounded to one decimal.
The sheet labels are used to enumerate every settled screen and represented variant, including transitions grouped with their destinations.
Static mid-entry frames demonstrate temporary transformations, opacity and clipping, but cannot establish duration, smoothness, flashing, performance or whether motion preferences were ignored.
The supplied narrative reports control measurements, but exact target bounds were not inspected. Small visible icons do not by themselves prove undersized touch targets.
Zero horizontal overflow and axe violations do not establish keyboard safe areas, readable contrast everywhere, logical focus order, screen-reader usability or complete text-enlargement support.

Physical iPhone Safari, native Dynamic Type, VoiceOver/TalkBack, microphone hardware, haptics, real payments, live social/auth backend and OS sharing remain unverified. No 9/10 certification is justified.
Synthetic headlines and repeated explanation text establish layout examples only. They provide no evidence of predictive accuracy, model quality or general semantic relevance.
No before/after change comparison, representative novice-use evidence or passed performance trace is supplied.
The authorized A>=9 and F>=9 threshold is not met by any evaluated screen or component. The weaker >=8 acceptance criterion is also not met throughout.
topFixes: Make the Approach instruction readable and distinguish its actionable target from decorative rings; it currently fails the essential-content gate.
Normalize question choices into one alignment, type scale and explicit selected treatment, especially card 2.
Reduce decorative height under text enlargement and keep question context, input and next action easier to reach together.
Clear content and primary actions above the raised tab-bar orb, particularly Sky; verify the last scrollable item remains fully accessible.
Preserve readable task context through transitions instead of rotating, shrinking or fading the entire control surface; verify reduced motion and performance.
Clarify credits remaining, reconcile the exhausted-plan balance, align prediction timing with due dates, and expose the intended check-in action.
Strengthen small secondary text and state cues, then verify actual targets, keyboard behavior and assistive technology on physical devices before seeking premium certification.
